topic: The mechanic certificate: eligibility, tests and privileges

notes.front: What is the mechanic certificate, and which ratings can it carry?
notes.back: The federal certificate for aviation maintenance technicians; it carries an airframe rating, a powerplant rating, or both.
notes.explanation: The two ratings can be gained separately or together as a combined certificate.
notes.example: Like a driving licence that can list more than one vehicle category on the same card, but for airframes and powerplants.
notes.source: FAA, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook – General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), ch. 13 “Mechanic Privileges & Limitations”, “Section 65.71, Eligibility Requirements: General”, p. 13-3
notes.evidence: The FAA recognizes two ratings: airframe and powerplant. These may be attained by a person upon successful application and testing either individually or as a combined certificate.

notes.front: What is an aviation maintenance technician school (AMTS)?
notes.back: A school certificated under part 147 of Title 14 whose certificate of completion can stand in for documented practical experience.
notes.explanation: A mechanic applicant needs either the school's completion document or documented practical experience.
notes.example: Like an approved training college whose diploma counts instead of years on the job, but for aircraft mechanics.
notes.source: FAA, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook – General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), ch. 13 “Mechanic Privileges & Limitations”, “Section 65.77, Experience Requirements”, p. 13-3
notes.evidence: Each mechanic applicant must have a certificate of completion from a certificated aviation maintenance technician school (AMTS) (14 CFR part 147) or provide documented evidence of a minimum of 18 months practical experience

notes.front: What is an inspection authorisation (IA)?
notes.back: An added authority for a certificated mechanic to perform annual inspections and approve work after major repairs or alterations.
notes.explanation: The IA may also perform or supervise a progressive inspection.
notes.example: Like a senior surveyor who may sign off a whole building, while other surveyors sign off only their own trade's work.
notes.source: FAA, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook – General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), ch. 13 “Mechanic Privileges & Limitations”, “Section 65.95, Inspection Authorization: Privileges”, p. 13-6
notes.evidence: The IA may perform an annual inspection or perform or supervise a progressive inspection. They may also approve for return to service any aircraft-related part or appliance that has undergone a major repair or alteration

notes.front: What is ethics in aviation maintenance, using the handbook's definition of ethics?
notes.back: Applying ethics, “the study of standards of conduct and moral judgment”, to maintenance work and decisions.
notes.explanation: The word comes from the Greek “ethos”, meaning character or custom.
notes.example: Like a shop quoting a customer its honest eight-week turnaround rather than a hopeful six weeks to win the job.
notes.source: FAA, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook – General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), ch. 13 “Mechanic Privileges & Limitations”, “Ethics”, p. 13-6
notes.evidence: The word “ethics” is actually a philosophical term that comes from the Greek word “ethos,” which means character or custom. So, it is logical that a current definition of ethics is “the study of standards of conduct and moral judgment.”

notes.front: How old must a person be to be eligible for a mechanic certificate?
notes.back: At least 18.
notes.explanation: Age is the first of the general eligibility requirements in § 65.71.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.71 Eligibility requirements: General
notes.evidence: (a) To be eligible for a mechanic certificate and associated ratings, a person must— (1) Be at least 18 years of age;

notes.front: What minimum age does the Companion Guide list for taking the Aviation Mechanic General written test?
notes.back: None: its test table shows “N/A” for age.
notes.explanation: The same table lists 60 questions, 2.0 hours and a passing score of 70 for the General written test.
notes.source: FAA, Companion Guide to the Aviation Mechanic ACS (FAA-G-ACS-1, with Changes 1 and 2), “Chapter 3: Written Test Description”, p. 12
notes.evidence: AMG Aviation Mechanic Technician - 60 N/A 2.0 70 General

notes.front: A 17-year-old school student meets every other requirement and passes all the mechanic tests. What can the Administrator not yet do?
notes.back: Issue the mechanic certificate
notes.explanation: Eligibility for the certificate itself requires being at least 18 years old.
notes.choices:
A) Issue the mechanic certificate
B) Let the student sit the Aviation Mechanic General written test
C) Record the student's passing grades
D) Let the student keep studying at the school
notes.choicesExplained: B (Let the student sit the Aviation Mechanic General written test): is allowed: the Companion Guide lists no minimum age for the General written test. C (Record the student's passing grades): is not restricted by age. D (Let the student keep studying at the school): has nothing to do with certificate eligibility.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.71 Eligibility requirements: General
notes.evidence: (a) To be eligible for a mechanic certificate and associated ratings, a person must— (1) Be at least 18 years of age;

notes.front: What English language ability must a mechanic applicant have?
notes.back: Be able to read, write, speak and understand English.
notes.explanation: The one exception is for applicants employed outside the United States by a U.S. air carrier.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.71 Eligibility requirements: General
notes.evidence: (2) Be able to read, write, speak, and understand the English language, or in the case of an applicant who does not meet this requirement and who is employed outside of the United States by a U.S. air carrier

notes.front: What endorsement does a mechanic certificate carry if the holder lacks the English requirement but is employed outside the United States by a U.S. air carrier?
notes.back: “Valid only outside the United States”.
notes.explanation: The endorsement lets such an applicant hold the certificate while limiting where it can be used.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.71 Eligibility requirements: General
notes.evidence: who is employed outside of the United States by a U.S. air carrier, have his certificate endorsed ‘‘Valid only outside the United States’’;

notes.front: An applicant employed at an overseas base of a U.S. air carrier cannot read or write English but otherwise qualifies. What happens?
notes.back: The certificate is issued endorsed “Valid only outside the United States”
notes.explanation: § 65.71 makes this exception only for applicants employed outside the United States by a U.S. air carrier.
notes.choices:
A) The certificate is refused outright
B) The certificate is issued endorsed “Valid only outside the United States”
C) A normal certificate is issued
D) A temporary certificate valid for 120 days is issued instead
notes.choicesExplained: A (The certificate is refused outright): ignores the exception for applicants employed abroad by a U.S. air carrier. C (A normal certificate is issued): would drop the required endorsement. D (A temporary certificate valid for 120 days is issued instead): confuses the rule with § 65.13 temporary certificates.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.71 Eligibility requirements: General
notes.evidence: who is employed outside of the United States by a U.S. air carrier, have his certificate endorsed ‘‘Valid only outside the United States’’;

notes.front: Within what period must a mechanic applicant pass all the prescribed tests?
notes.back: Within a period of 24 months.
notes.explanation: Every prescribed test must fall inside that one 24-month period.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.71 Eligibility requirements: General
notes.evidence: (3) Have passed all of the prescribed tests within a period of 24 months;

notes.front: According to the Companion Guide, when does a mechanic's written (knowledge) test report expire?
notes.back: 24 calendar months after the month in which the written test was completed.
notes.explanation: If it expires before the practical test is complete, the written test must be retaken and passed.
notes.source: FAA, Companion Guide to the Aviation Mechanic ACS (FAA-G-ACS-1, with Changes 1 and 2), “Chapter 4: Practical Test Description”, p. 19
notes.evidence: An AKTR expires 24 calendar months after the month the applicant completes the written test pursuant to 14 CFR part 65, section 65.71(a)(3) and (b). If the AKTR expires before completion of the practical test, the applicant must retake, pass, and present the AKTR

notes.front: An applicant passes the Aviation Mechanic General written test on 10 March 2025. Going by the Companion Guide, when does that test report expire?
notes.back: At the end of March 2027
notes.explanation: The report runs for 24 calendar months after the month of the test, so March 2025 carries it to the end of March 2027.
notes.choices:
A) At the end of March 2026
B) At the end of September 2026
C) At the end of March 2027
D) Never; written results do not expire
notes.choicesExplained: A (At the end of March 2026): allows only 12 months. B (At the end of September 2026): allows only 18 months. D (Never; written results do not expire): ignores the 24-month limit.
notes.source: FAA, Companion Guide to the Aviation Mechanic ACS (FAA-G-ACS-1, with Changes 1 and 2), “Chapter 4: Practical Test Description”, p. 19
notes.evidence: An AKTR expires 24 calendar months after the month the applicant completes the written test

notes.front: What must a certificated mechanic do to add the other rating?
notes.back: Meet the § 65.77 experience requirements and, within 24 calendar months, pass the written, oral and practical tests for it.
notes.explanation: The tests are those of §§ 65.75 and 65.79, taken for the rating being added.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.71 Eligibility requirements: General
notes.evidence: (b) A certificated mechanic who applies for an additional rating must meet the requirements of § 65.77 and, within a period of 24 calendar months, pass the tests prescribed by §§ 65.75 and 65.79 for the additional rating sought

notes.front: Under § 65.75(a), when does a mechanic applicant normally take the written test?
notes.back: After meeting the § 65.77 experience requirements.
notes.explanation: Paragraph (c) of the same section provides the exception.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.75 Knowledge requirements
notes.evidence: (a) Except as specified in paragraph (c) of this section, each applicant for a mechanic certificate or rating must, after meeting the applicable experience requirements of § 65.77, pass a written test, appropriate to the rating sought

notes.front: What must an applicant pass before applying for the oral and practical tests?
notes.back: Each section of the written test.
notes.explanation: A report of the written test is then sent to the applicant.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.75 Knowledge requirements
notes.evidence: (b) The applicant must pass each section of the test before applying for the oral and practical tests prescribed by § 65.79. A report of the written test is sent to the applicant.

notes.front: Under § 65.75(c), what lets an applicant take the mechanic general written test before meeting the experience requirements?
notes.back: An authenticated AMTS document showing satisfactory completion of the general portion of the curriculum, with the completion date.
notes.explanation: It is the one exception to taking the written test only after meeting experience.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.75 Knowledge requirements
notes.evidence: may take the mechanic general written test prior to meeting the applicable experience requirements of § 65.77, provided the applicant presents an authenticated document from a certificated aviation maintenance technician school that demonstrates satisfactory completion of the general portion of the school’s curriculum and specifies the completion date.

notes.front: Must an AMTS give students a document showing completion of the general portion of its curriculum?
notes.back: No, it is not required to.
notes.explanation: If the school does not issue one, the student is not eligible to take the general written test early.
notes.source: FAA, Companion Guide to the Aviation Mechanic ACS (FAA-G-ACS-1, with Changes 1 and 2), “Authorization for AMTS Students to Take General Written Test Early”, p. 9
notes.evidence: an AMTS is not required to provide authenticated documentation that demonstrates satisfactory completion of the general portion of the school’s curriculum. The FAA notes that if the AMTS does not issue such a document, then the student will not be eligible to take the general written test early.

notes.front: An AMTS student has finished the general portion of the course but has no practical experience. The school issues an authenticated document stating the completion date. What may the student do?
notes.back: Take the mechanic general written test now
notes.explanation: § 65.75(c) allows the general written test before the experience requirements are met when such a document is presented.
notes.choices:
A) Take all three written tests now
B) Nothing until graduation
C) Take the general written test after 18 months of work experience
D) Take the mechanic general written test now
notes.choicesExplained: A (Take all three written tests now): goes too far: § 65.75(c) covers only the general written test. B (Nothing until graduation): ignores the § 65.75(c) exception. C (Take the general written test after 18 months of work experience): describes the normal route, which this student does not need.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.75 Knowledge requirements
notes.evidence: may take the mechanic general written test prior to meeting the applicable experience requirements of § 65.77, provided the applicant presents an authenticated document from a certificated aviation maintenance technician school

notes.front: Under § 65.75(d), when may an applicant take the mechanic practical test with an expired written test report?
notes.back: When they qualify under the relief in § 61.40.
notes.explanation: Section 61.40 sets out who qualifies for the relief.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.75 Knowledge requirements
notes.evidence: (d) An applicant is eligible to take a practical test for a mechanic certificate or rating under this part with an expired written test report in accordance with § 61.40 of this chapter.

notes.front: Who does the § 61.40 relief for expired written test reports cover?
notes.back: U.S. military and civilian personnel assigned outside the United States in support of U.S. Armed Forces operations.
notes.explanation: The relief is aimed at people serving abroad in support of U.S. Armed Forces operations.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.40 (eCFR, current text)
notes.evidence: Relief for U.S. Military and civilian personnel who are assigned outside the United States in support of U.S. Armed Forces operations.

notes.front: Without an AMTS document, how much practical experience must an applicant document for one rating?
notes.back: At least 18 months, with the procedures, practices, materials, tools and equipment used on airframes or powerplants.
notes.explanation: The experience must be appropriate to the rating sought.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.77 Experience requirements
notes.evidence: (1) At least 18 months of practical experience with the procedures, practices, materials, tools, machine tools, and equipment generally used in constructing, maintaining, or altering air- frames or powerplants, appropriate to the rating sought;

notes.front: How much practical experience qualifies an applicant for both the airframe and powerplant ratings?
notes.back: At least 30 months concurrently performing the duties of both ratings.
notes.explanation: The duties of both ratings must be performed concurrently over that time.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.77 Experience requirements
notes.evidence: (2) At least 30 months of practical experience concurrently performing the duties appropriate to both the airframe and powerplant ratings.

notes.front: With no school document, an applicant has 20 months of documented airframe experience and none on powerplants. What can they apply for?
notes.back: The airframe rating only
notes.explanation: 18 months of experience appropriate to the rating sought is enough for that one rating.
notes.choices:
A) The airframe rating only
B) Both ratings
C) The powerplant rating only
D) Neither rating yet
notes.choicesExplained: B (Both ratings): needs 30 months concurrently doing the duties of both. C (The powerplant rating only): needs experience appropriate to powerplants. D (Neither rating yet): overlooks that 18 months meets the requirement for one rating.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.77 Experience requirements
notes.evidence: (1) At least 18 months of practical experience with the procedures, practices, materials, tools, machine tools, and equipment generally used in constructing, maintaining, or altering air- frames or powerplants, appropriate to the rating sought; or (2) At least 30 months of practical experience concurrently performing the duties appropriate to both

notes.front: What is the alternative to documented practical experience under § 65.77?
notes.back: An authenticated document from a certificated AMTS, issued under § 147.21.
notes.explanation: § 65.77 lets an applicant present either this document or documentary evidence of experience.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.77 Experience requirements
notes.evidence: Each applicant for a mechanic certificate or rating must present either— (a) An authenticated document from a certificated aviation maintenance technician school in accordance with § 147.21 of this chapter;

notes.front: What does § 65.79 require of every mechanic applicant?
notes.back: Passing an oral test and a practical test for the rating sought.
notes.explanation: The applicant shows satisfactory understanding of the ACS knowledge, risk management and skill elements for each subject.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.79 Skill requirements
notes.evidence: Each applicant for a mechanic certificate or rating must pass an oral test and a practical test, as appropriate to the rating sought, by demonstrating satisfactory understanding of the knowledge, risk management, and skill elements for each subject

notes.front: According to the Companion Guide, on which tests are ACS knowledge elements assessed?
notes.back: The written test and the oral test.
notes.explanation: Knowledge elements are the ones worded “Exhibits knowledge in…”.
notes.source: FAA, Companion Guide to the Aviation Mechanic ACS (FAA-G-ACS-1, with Changes 1 and 2), “Chapter 2: How to Use the ACS”, p. 11
notes.evidence: Knowledge—(written test, oral test) elements are indicated by use of the words, "Exhibits knowledge in..."

notes.front: According to the Companion Guide, on which tests are ACS risk management elements assessed?
notes.back: The oral test and the practical test.
notes.explanation: Risk elements are the ones worded with “Determine, Identify, Creates…”.
notes.source: FAA, Companion Guide to the Aviation Mechanic ACS (FAA-G-ACS-1, with Changes 1 and 2), “Chapter 2: How to Use the ACS”, p. 11
notes.evidence: Risk—(oral test, practical test) elements are indicated by the use of the words, “Determine, Identify, Creates…"

notes.front: According to the Companion Guide, on which test are ACS skill elements assessed?
notes.back: The practical test.
notes.explanation: Skill elements are the ones worded “Demonstrates the skill to perform…”.
notes.source: FAA, Companion Guide to the Aviation Mechanic ACS (FAA-G-ACS-1, with Changes 1 and 2), “Chapter 2: How to Use the ACS”, p. 11
notes.evidence: Skill—(practical test) elements are indicated by the use of the words, "Demonstrates the skill to perform..."

notes.front: Does the Aviation Mechanic General written test assess ACS risk management elements?
notes.back: No: the written test covers knowledge elements; risk elements are assessed on the oral and practical tests.
notes.explanation: The Companion Guide maps knowledge to the written and oral tests, and risk to the oral and practical tests.
notes.source: FAA, Companion Guide to the Aviation Mechanic ACS (FAA-G-ACS-1, with Changes 1 and 2), “Chapter 2: How to Use the ACS”, p. 11
notes.evidence: Knowledge—(written test, oral test) elements are indicated by use of the words, "Exhibits knowledge in..." • Risk—(oral test, practical test) elements

notes.front: Under § 65.80, when may an AMTS student take the oral and practical tests?
notes.back: During the final subjects of their training, once the school shows they are ready.
notes.explanation: This can come before the experience requirements are met and before each written section is passed.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.80 Certificated aviation maintenance technician school students
notes.evidence: that student may take those tests during the final subjects of the student’s training in the curriculum required under part 147, before the student meets the applicable experience requirements of § 65.77 and before the student passes each section of the written test

notes.front: An AMTS shows the Administrator that a student in the final subjects has made satisfactory progress and is ready for the oral and practical tests. The student has not yet passed the written tests. What may the student do?
notes.back: Take the oral and practical tests now
notes.explanation: § 65.80 lets such a student take both tests before passing each written section.
notes.choices:
A) Nothing until each written section is passed
B) Take the oral and practical tests now
C) Only the oral test, not the practical
D) Take the tests only after 18 months of work experience
notes.choicesExplained: A (Nothing until each written section is passed): is the normal § 65.75(b) order, which § 65.80 sets aside for such students. C (Only the oral test, not the practical): splits the tests; § 65.80 allows both. D (Take the tests only after 18 months of work experience): ignores that § 65.80 applies before experience is met.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.80 Certificated aviation maintenance technician school students
notes.evidence: shows to the Administrator that any of its students has made satisfactory progress at the school and is prepared to take the oral and practical tests prescribed by § 65.79, that student may take those tests

notes.front: How many questions does the Aviation Mechanic General written test have, and how long is allowed?
notes.back: 60 questions in 2.0 hours.
notes.explanation: The Airframe test, by comparison, has 100 questions in the same 2.0 hours.
notes.source: FAA, Companion Guide to the Aviation Mechanic ACS (FAA-G-ACS-1, with Changes 1 and 2), “Chapter 3: Written Test Description”, p. 12
notes.evidence: AMG Aviation Mechanic Technician - 60 N/A 2.0 70 General AMA Aviation Mechanic Technician - 100 N/A 2.0 70 Airframe

notes.front: How do the Airframe and Powerplant written tests differ in size from the General written test?
notes.back: They have 100 questions each, against the General written test's 60, with the same 2.0 hours.
notes.explanation: Both also have a passing score of 70.
notes.source: FAA, Companion Guide to the Aviation Mechanic ACS (FAA-G-ACS-1, with Changes 1 and 2), “Chapter 3: Written Test Description”, p. 12
notes.evidence: AMA Aviation Mechanic Technician - 100 N/A 2.0 70 Airframe AMP Aviation Mechanic Technician - 100 N/A 2.0 70 Powerplant

notes.front: What share of General-test questions does the Companion Guide's blueprint give to Mathematics?
notes.explanation: Cleaning and Corrosion Control carries the same 5–10% range.
notes.source: FAA, Companion Guide to the Aviation Mechanic ACS (FAA-G-ACS-1, with Changes 1 and 2), “Written Test Blueprints”, p. 13
notes.evidence: Cleaning and Corrosion Control 5 - 10% Mathematics 5 - 10%

notes.front: Which two General-test knowledge areas have the widest blueprint range, 5–15%?
notes.back: Fundamentals of Electricity and Electronics, and Ground Operations and Servicing.
notes.explanation: Areas such as Aircraft Drawings and Weight and Balance are listed at 5–10%.
notes.source: FAA, Companion Guide to the Aviation Mechanic ACS (FAA-G-ACS-1, with Changes 1 and 2), “Written Test Blueprints”, p. 13
notes.evidence: Fundamentals of Electricity and Electronics 5 - 15% Aircraft Drawings 5 - 10% Weight and Balance 5 - 10% Fluid Lines and Fittings 5 - 10% Aircraft Materials, Hardware, and Processes 5 - 10% Ground Operations and Servicing 5 - 15%

notes.front: What is the minimum passing grade for each test under part 65?
notes.back: 70 percent.
notes.explanation: The same minimum applies to each test given under part 65.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.17 Tests: General procedure
notes.evidence: (b) The minimum passing grade for each test is 70 percent.

notes.front: What is the penalty for cheating or other unauthorised conduct on a part 65 written test?
notes.back: No airman certificate or rating for 1 year after the act, and grounds to suspend or revoke any held.
notes.explanation: The ineligibility runs from the date of the prohibited act.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.18 Written tests: Cheating or other unauthorized conduct
notes.evidence: (b) No person who commits an act prohibited by paragraph (a) of this section is eligible for any airman or ground instructor certificate or rating under this chapter for a period of 1 year after the date of that act. In addition, the commission of that act is a basis for suspending or revoking

notes.front: What are two acts § 65.18 prohibits during a written test, unless the Administrator authorises them?
notes.back: Any two of: giving or receiving help; taking it for someone else; using any material or aid (among others).
notes.explanation: Help is barred in both directions, given and received.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.18 Written tests: Cheating or other unauthorized conduct
notes.evidence: (3) Give help on that test to, or receive help on that test from, any person during the period that test is being given; (4) Take any part of that test in behalf of another person; (5) Use any material or aid during the period that test is being given;

notes.front: During the General written test, a proctor finds an applicant using a sheet of formulas brought from home without authorisation. What follows under part 65?
notes.back: No airman certificate or rating for 1 year after the act
notes.explanation: Using any material or aid during the test is a prohibited act, which bars any airman certificate or rating for 1 year.
notes.choices:
A) A retest after 30 days
B) A retest after 90 days
C) No airman certificate or rating for 1 year after the act
D) Only the formula sheet is confiscated
notes.choicesExplained: A (A retest after 30 days): is the ordinary rule for failing, not for cheating. B (A retest after 90 days): is the wait after failing the inspection authorisation test. D (Only the formula sheet is confiscated): ignores the 1-year ineligibility in § 65.18(b).
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.18 Written tests: Cheating or other unauthorized conduct
notes.evidence: (b) No person who commits an act prohibited by paragraph (a) of this section is eligible for any airman or ground instructor certificate or rating under this chapter for a period of 1 year after the date of that act.

notes.front: After failing a written, oral or practical test, when may a mechanic applicant retest?
notes.back: After 30 days, or sooner with a signed statement from an airman holding the certificate and rating sought.
notes.explanation: The two routes are alternatives: wait out the 30 days, or bring the statement.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.19 Retesting after failure
notes.evidence: (a) After 30 days after the date the applicant failed the test; or (b) Before the 30 days have expired if the applicant presents a signed statement from an airman holding the certificate and rating sought by the applicant

notes.front: Once the 30-day wait after a failure has passed, is a signed statement of extra training still needed to retest?
notes.back: No.
notes.explanation: The signed statement only matters for retesting before the 30 days are up.
notes.source: FAA, Companion Guide to the Aviation Mechanic ACS (FAA-G-ACS-1, with Changes 1 and 2), “Retests”, p. 10
notes.evidence: After a 30-day waiting period for retesting, a signed statement of additional training is not required.

notes.front: An applicant fails the General written test and wants to retest next week. What will allow that?
notes.back: A signed statement from a mechanic holding the certificate and rating sought, certifying extra instruction and readiness
notes.explanation: Retesting before 30 days needs that airman's signed statement covering each failed subject.
notes.choices:
A) A flight instructor's logbook endorsement
B) Nothing; a 90-day wait always applies
C) A new Form 8610-2 signed by the testing centre
D) A signed statement from a mechanic holding the certificate and rating sought, certifying extra instruction and readiness
notes.choicesExplained: A (A flight instructor's logbook endorsement): is a pilot rule; part 65 asks for an airman holding the certificate and rating sought. B (Nothing; a 90-day wait always applies): is the inspection authorisation retest rule. C (A new Form 8610-2 signed by the testing centre): is not what § 65.19 requires.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.19 Retesting after failure
notes.evidence: presents a signed statement from an airman holding the certificate and rating sought by the applicant, certifying that the airman has given the applicant additional instruction in each of the subjects failed and that the airman considers the applicant ready for retesting.

notes.front: How does retesting after failing the IA test differ from retesting after failing a mechanic test?
notes.back: The IA wait is at least 90 days with no reduction for training; the mechanic wait is 30 days and can be shortened.
notes.explanation: Extra training shortens only the mechanic test wait, not the IA wait.
notes.source: FAA, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook – General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), ch. 13 “Mechanic Privileges & Limitations”, “Section 65.91, Inspection Authorization”, p. 13-5
notes.evidence: If the applicant fails the test, retesting cannot be attempted until a minimum of 90 days have elapsed from the failure date. Unlike the A&P test, there is no reduction in this time if the applicant receives additional training.

notes.front: What are two acts § 65.20 forbids concerning part 65 applications, records and certificates?
notes.back: Reproducing a certificate or rating for a fraudulent purpose, and any alteration of one (among others).
notes.explanation: Alteration is barred whatever the purpose; reproduction is barred when done for a fraudulent purpose.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.20 Falsification, reproduction, or alteration
notes.evidence: (3) Any reproduction, for fraudulent purpose, of any certificate or rating under this part; or (4) Any alteration of any certificate or rating under this part.

notes.front: Within what time, and how, must a certificate holder report a change of permanent mailing address?
notes.back: Within 30 days, in writing, to the Airman Certification Branch.
notes.explanation: The rule requires written notice and gives the Branch's postal address in Oklahoma City.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.21 Change of address
notes.evidence: Within 30 days after any change in his permanent mailing address, the holder of a certificate issued under this part shall notify the Department of Transportation, Federal Aviation Administration, Airman Certification Branch, Post Office Box 25082, Oklahoma City, OK 73125, in writing, of his new address.

notes.front: A mechanic moves to a new permanent address on 1 June. What must they do?
notes.back: Notify the Airman Certification Branch in writing within 30 days
notes.explanation: § 65.21 sets 30 days and requires written notice to the Airman Certification Branch.
notes.choices:
A) Notify the Airman Certification Branch in writing within 30 days
B) Phone the local Flight Standards office within 60 days
C) Nothing until the certificate is renewed
D) Write the new address on the certificate
notes.choicesExplained: B (Phone the local Flight Standards office within 60 days): has the wrong method and the wrong time. C (Nothing until the certificate is renewed): wrongly assumes the certificate is renewed. D (Write the new address on the certificate): would be an alteration of the certificate, forbidden by § 65.20.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.21 Change of address
notes.evidence: Within 30 days after any change in his permanent mailing address, the holder of a certificate issued under this part shall notify

notes.front: For how long may a temporary certificate be issued under § 65.13?
notes.back: Not more than 120 days.
notes.explanation: It covers the applicant while the Administrator reviews the application and issues the permanent certificate.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.13 Temporary certificate
notes.evidence: A certificate and ratings effective for a period of not more than 120 days may be issued to a qualified applicant, pending review of his application and supplementary documents

notes.front: A new mechanic's temporary certificate reaches its 120-day end and the permanent certificate has not arrived. What does the Companion Guide say to do?
notes.back: Contact the local Flight Standards Office
notes.explanation: The guide tells an airman whose temporary certificate expires before the certificate is issued to contact their local Flight Standards Office.
notes.choices:
A) Keep working on the expired temporary certificate
B) Contact the local Flight Standards Office
C) Retake the practical test
D) Ask the examiner to extend it by hand
notes.choicesExplained: A (Keep working on the expired temporary certificate): ignores that it has run out. C (Retake the practical test): is not required; the tests were passed. D (Ask the examiner to extend it by hand): is not an option the guide gives.
notes.source: FAA, Companion Guide to the Aviation Mechanic ACS (FAA-G-ACS-1, with Changes 1 and 2), “Temporary Certificate”, p. 24
notes.evidence: The temporary certificate is valid for 120 days from the date of issuance. If the temporary certificate expires before the airman’s certificate is issued, the airman should contact their local Flight Standards Office

notes.front: How long is a mechanic certificate effective?
notes.back: Until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked.
notes.explanation: Repairman certificates are the one exception to this rule.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.15 Duration of certificates
notes.evidence: (a) Except for repairman certificates, a certificate or rating issued under this part is effective until it is surrendered, suspended, or revoked.

notes.front: As the handbook defines them, what do “surrendered” and “suspended” mean for a certificate?
notes.back: Surrendered: given up voluntarily. Suspended: the Administrator temporarily removes it from the holder.
notes.explanation: The difference is who acts: the holder surrenders a certificate, the Administrator suspends it.
notes.source: FAA, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook – General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), ch. 13 “Mechanic Privileges & Limitations”, “Section 65.15, Duration of Certificates”, p. 13-2
notes.evidence: Surrendered means given up voluntarily. • • Suspended means the FAA temporarily removes the certificate from the holder.

notes.front: After an enforcement case, the Administrator permanently removes a mechanic's certificate. Which term describes this?
notes.back: Revoked
notes.explanation: Revocation is the permanent removal of the certificate by the Administrator.
notes.choices:
A) Suspended
B) Surrendered
C) Revoked
D) Expired
notes.choicesExplained: A (Suspended): is a temporary removal. B (Surrendered): means the holder gave it up voluntarily. D (Expired): does not apply: a mechanic certificate has no expiry date.
notes.source: FAA, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook – General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), ch. 13 “Mechanic Privileges & Limitations”, “Section 65.15, Duration of Certificates”, p. 13-2
notes.evidence: Revoked means the FAA permanently removes the certificate from the holder.

notes.front: After what date may the holder of a paper part 65 certificate (other than a temporary one) no longer exercise its privileges?
notes.back: After 31 March 2013.
notes.explanation: Temporary certificates issued under § 65.13 are excepted.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.15 Duration of certificates
notes.evidence: the holder of a paper certificate issued under this part may not exercise the privileges of that certificate after March 31, 2013.

notes.front: What can a conviction under a federal or state drug statute lead to for a part 65 applicant or holder?
notes.back: Denial of an application for up to 1 year after final conviction, or suspension or revocation of certificates held.
notes.explanation: The conviction is grounds for either outcome.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.12 Offenses involving alcohol or drugs
notes.evidence: is grounds for— (1) Denial of an application for any certificate or rating issued under this part for a period of up to 1 year after the date of final conviction; or (2) Suspension or revocation of any certificate or rating issued under this part.

notes.front: After a mechanic certificate is revoked, how long before the person may apply for a mechanic or repairman certificate?
notes.back: 1 year after the date of revocation.
notes.explanation: The bar covers both kinds of certificate, not just the one revoked.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.11 Application and issue
notes.evidence: (2) A person whose mechanic or repairman certificate is revoked may not apply for either of those kinds of certificates for 1 year after the date of revocation.

notes.front: While a mechanic certificate is suspended, may the holder apply for a rating to be added to it?
notes.back: No, unless the Administrator authorises it.
notes.explanation: The bar lasts for the period of the suspension.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.11 Application and issue
notes.evidence: (c) Unless authorized by the Administrator, a person whose air traffic control tower operator, mechanic, or parachute rigger certificate is suspended may not apply for any rating to be added to that certificate during the period of suspension.

notes.front: Under § 65.81(a), what may a certificated mechanic do?
notes.back: Perform or supervise the maintenance, preventive maintenance or alteration of aircraft or appliances for which they are rated.
notes.explanation: The privilege covers both doing the work and supervising it.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.81 General privileges and limitations
notes.evidence: (a) A certificated mechanic may perform or supervise the maintenance, preventive maintenance or alteration of an aircraft or appliance, or a part thereof, for which he is rated

notes.front: Which propeller work does § 65.81(a) exclude from a mechanic's general privileges?
notes.back: Major repairs to, and major alterations of, propellers.
notes.explanation: The same clause also excludes any repair or alteration of instruments.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.81 General privileges and limitations
notes.evidence: (but excluding major repairs to, and major alterations of, propellers, and any repair to, or alteration of, instruments)

notes.front: Which instrument work does § 65.81(a) exclude from a mechanic's privileges?
notes.back: Any repair to, or alteration of, instruments.
notes.explanation: Unlike the propeller exclusion, this one is not limited to major work.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.81 General privileges and limitations
notes.evidence: (but excluding major repairs to, and major alterations of, propellers, and any repair to, or alteration of, instruments)

notes.front: According to the handbook, who does the propeller and instrument work excluded from mechanics?
notes.back: Certificated repairmen at an authorised repair station.
notes.explanation: The handbook says these activities are reserved for them.
notes.source: FAA, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook – General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), ch. 13 “Mechanic Privileges & Limitations”, “Section 65.81, General Privileges and Limitations”, p. 13-4
notes.evidence: These activities are reserved for certificated repairmen at an authorized repair station.

notes.front: Which task is outside the privileges of a mechanic holding both airframe and powerplant ratings?
notes.back: Repairing a flight instrument
notes.explanation: § 65.81(a) excludes any repair to, or alteration of, instruments.
notes.choices:
A) Replacing a hydraulic line on the airframe
B) Performing a 100-hour inspection on the engine
C) Making a minor repair to a propeller
D) Repairing a flight instrument
notes.choicesExplained: A (Replacing a hydraulic line on the airframe): is airframe maintenance for which the mechanic is rated. B (Performing a 100-hour inspection on the engine): is a powerplant rating privilege. C (Making a minor repair to a propeller): is allowed; only major repairs and alterations of propellers are excluded.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.81 General privileges and limitations
notes.evidence: (but excluding major repairs to, and major alterations of, propellers, and any repair to, or alteration of, instruments)

notes.front: What must a mechanic have done before supervising, or approving for return to service, a task they are rated for?
notes.back: Performed that work satisfactorily at an earlier date.
notes.explanation: Being rated is not enough on its own; the specific work must have been done before.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.81 General privileges and limitations
notes.evidence: any aircraft or appliance, or part thereof, for which he is rated unless he has satisfactorily performed the work concerned at an earlier date.

notes.front: If a mechanic has never done a task, how can they show they are able to do it?
notes.back: Perform it to the Administrator's satisfaction, or under direct supervision of an appropriately rated, experienced mechanic or repairman.
notes.explanation: The supervisor must have previous experience in that specific operation.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.81 General privileges and limitations
notes.evidence: he may show his ability to do it by performing it to the satisfaction of the Administrator or under the direct supervision of a certificated and appropriately rated mechanic, or a certificated repairman, who has had previous experience in the specific operation concerned.

notes.front: A newly certificated airframe mechanic is asked to supervise a fabric recovering job they have never done. What should happen first?
notes.back: They do the work under direct supervision of an appropriately rated mechanic experienced in it, or to the Administrator's satisfaction
notes.explanation: § 65.81(a) bars supervising work not satisfactorily performed at an earlier date, and names these two ways to show ability.
notes.choices:
A) They do the work under direct supervision of an appropriately rated mechanic experienced in it, or to the Administrator's satisfaction
B) They supervise it now, because they hold the airframe rating
C) They must first obtain an inspection authorisation
D) They must first get 6 more months of recent experience
notes.choicesExplained: B (They supervise it now, because they hold the airframe rating): ignores the earlier-performance rule. C (They must first obtain an inspection authorisation): is not the requirement; the IA is a separate authority. D (They must first get 6 more months of recent experience): confuses this rule with § 65.83.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.81 General privileges and limitations
notes.evidence: he may show his ability to do it by performing it to the satisfaction of the Administrator or under the direct supervision of a certificated and appropriately rated mechanic, or a certificated repairman, who has had previous experience in the specific operation concerned.

notes.front: Under § 65.81(b), what must a mechanic understand before exercising their privileges on a task?
notes.back: The current manufacturer's instructions and maintenance manuals for that specific operation.
notes.explanation: The requirement is tied to the specific operation, not to general knowledge.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.81 General privileges and limitations
notes.evidence: (b) A certificated mechanic may not exercise the privileges of his certificate and rating unless he understands the current instructions of the manufacturer, and the maintenance manuals, for the specific operation concerned.

notes.front: A mechanic who has often replaced a fuel pump finds the manufacturer has revised the procedure. What must they do before doing the job?
notes.back: Understand the current manufacturer's instructions and manuals for that operation
notes.explanation: § 65.81(b) ties the privileges to understanding the current instructions for the specific operation.
notes.choices:
A) Nothing; having done it before is enough
B) Understand the current manufacturer's instructions and manuals for that operation
C) Get an inspection authorisation
D) Retake the practical test
notes.choicesExplained: A (Nothing; having done it before is enough): overlooks § 65.81(b), which requires the current instructions. C (Get an inspection authorisation): is not required for this work. D (Retake the practical test): is not required for a revised procedure.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.81 General privileges and limitations
notes.evidence: unless he understands the current instructions of the manufacturer, and the maintenance manuals, for the specific operation concerned.

notes.front: What recent experience must a mechanic have to exercise their privileges?
notes.back: Within the preceding 24 months, at least 6 months of qualifying work, or the Administrator finding them able to do the work.
notes.explanation: Either route, a finding by the Administrator or 6 months of work, satisfies the rule.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.83 Recent experience requirements
notes.evidence: A certificated mechanic may not exercise the privileges of his certificate and rating unless, within the preceding 24 months— (a) The Administrator has found that he is able to do that work; or (b) He has, for at least 6 months—

notes.front: Which three activities (alone or combined) count towards a mechanic's 6 months of recent experience?
notes.back: Serving as a mechanic under the certificate; technically supervising other mechanics; supervising aircraft maintenance in an executive capacity.
notes.explanation: Any combination of the three also counts.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.83 Recent experience requirements
notes.evidence: (1) Served as a mechanic under his certificate and rating; (2) Technically supervised other mechanics; (3) Supervised, in an executive capacity, the maintenance or alteration of aircraft; or (4) Been engaged in any combination of paragraph (b) (1), (2), or (3) of this section.

notes.front: In the last 24 months a mechanic worked 4 months as a mechanic and then 3 months technically supervising other mechanics. Can they exercise their privileges?
notes.back: Yes; the combination gives 7 months of qualifying activity
notes.explanation: § 65.83(b)(4) counts any combination of the three activities towards the 6 months.
notes.choices:
A) No; 6 months of hands-on mechanic work alone is needed
B) No; supervising does not count
C) Yes; the combination gives 7 months of qualifying activity
D) Only after a finding by the Administrator of ability
notes.choicesExplained: A (No; 6 months of hands-on mechanic work alone is needed): ignores that combinations count. B (No; supervising does not count): ignores § 65.83(b)(2). D (Only after a finding by the Administrator of ability): is needed only when the 6 months are not met.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.83 Recent experience requirements
notes.evidence: (4) Been engaged in any combination of paragraph (b) (1), (2), or (3) of this section.

notes.front: A mechanic spent the last 30 months flying as a pilot and did no maintenance work. What is the position?
notes.back: The certificate is still valid, but its privileges cannot be used until the recent experience rule is met again
notes.explanation: § 65.83 blocks the privileges without 6 months' qualifying work in the preceding 24 months or a finding by the Administrator of ability.
notes.choices:
A) The certificate has expired and must be re-earned
B) Nothing changes; privileges continue
C) The certificate is automatically suspended
D) The certificate is still valid, but its privileges cannot be used until the recent experience rule is met again
notes.choicesExplained: A (The certificate has expired and must be re-earned): is wrong: it lasts until surrendered, suspended or revoked. B (Nothing changes; privileges continue): ignores § 65.83. C (The certificate is automatically suspended): is wrong: suspension is an Administrator action, not automatic.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.83 Recent experience requirements
notes.evidence: A certificated mechanic may not exercise the privileges of his certificate and rating unless, within the preceding 24 months— (a) The Administrator has found that he is able to do that work;

notes.front: The handbook says the certificate is valid until surrendered, suspended or revoked. What is the catch?
notes.back: It may not be exercised unless the holder has recently worked as a mechanic (6 of the preceding 24 months).
notes.explanation: Validity and the right to use the privileges are separate questions.
notes.source: FAA, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook – General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), ch. 13 “Mechanic Privileges & Limitations”, “Section 65.83, Recent Experience Requirements”, p. 13-4
notes.evidence: the A&P certificate is valid until it is surrendered, suspended, or revoked, it may not be exercised if the holder has not been actively working as a mechanic for at least 6 of

notes.front: What may an airframe-rated mechanic approve for return to service under § 65.85(a)?
notes.back: An airframe, part or appliance after performing, supervising or inspecting its maintenance or alteration, excluding major repairs and alterations.
notes.explanation: Major repairs and major alterations are outside this privilege.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.85 Airframe rating; additional privileges
notes.evidence: a certificated mechanic with an airframe rating may approve and return to service an airframe, or any related part or appliance, after he has performed, supervised, or inspected its maintenance or alteration (excluding major repairs and major alterations).

notes.front: Which part 91 inspection may an airframe-rated mechanic perform and approve for return to service?
notes.back: The 100-hour inspection on an airframe or related part or appliance.
notes.explanation: The inspection is the one required by part 91.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.85 Airframe rating; additional privileges
notes.evidence: In addition, he may perform the 100-hour inspection required by part 91 of this chapter on an airframe, or any related part or appliance, and approve and return it to service.

notes.front: What does the powerplant rating let a mechanic approve for return to service?
notes.back: A powerplant or propeller after their maintenance or alteration (not major work), and a 100-hour inspection on either.
notes.explanation: The propeller is covered by this rating as well as the powerplant.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.87 Powerplant rating; additional privileges
notes.evidence: a certificated mechanic with a powerplant rating may approve and return to service a powerplant or propeller or any related part or appliance, after he has performed, supervised, or inspected its maintenance or alteration (excluding major repairs and major alterations). In addition, he may perform the 100-hour inspection required by part 91

notes.front: According to the handbook, when an airframe mechanic does a major repair, who must do the return to service?
notes.back: A certificated mechanic holding an IA; the airframe mechanic may do the work and start the Form 337.
notes.explanation: Doing the work and approving it are split between the two people.
notes.source: FAA, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook – General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), ch. 13 “Mechanic Privileges & Limitations”, “Section 65.85, Airframe Rating: Additional Privileges”, p. 13-4
notes.evidence: They may also perform the maintenance actions required for a major repair or alteration, and should initiate the appropriate form (FAA Form 337, Major Repair and Alteration) associated with that work. However, the return to service action must be accomplished by a certificated A&P technician holding an Inspection Authorization (IA).

notes.front: For an aircraft with a special airworthiness certificate in the light-sport category, what extra privilege does an airframe or powerplant rating give?
notes.back: Approving return to service after performing and inspecting a major repair or alteration on products not produced under an approval from the Administrator.
notes.explanation: The work must follow instructions from the manufacturer or a person acceptable to the Administrator.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.85 Airframe rating; additional privileges
notes.evidence: (b) A certificated mechanic with an airframe rating can approve and return to service an airframe, or any related part or appliance, of an aircraft with a special airworthiness certificate in the light-sport category after performing and inspecting a major repair or major alteration for products that are not produced under an FAA approval

notes.front: Which of the 100-hour and annual inspections may a mechanic without an IA perform?
notes.back: The 100-hour inspection only; the annual inspection is an IA privilege.
notes.explanation: The ratings grant the 100-hour inspection, while § 65.95 gives the annual to IA holders.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.95 Inspection authorization: Privileges and limitations
notes.evidence: (2) Perform an annual, or perform or supervise a progressive inspection according to §§ 43.13 and 43.15 of this chapter.

notes.front: An owner asks a mechanic with airframe and powerplant ratings, but no IA, to do the aircraft's annual inspection. What can the mechanic offer?
notes.back: A 100-hour inspection, but not the annual
notes.explanation: Both ratings allow the 100-hour inspection; performing an annual is a privilege of the IA holder.
notes.choices:
A) A 100-hour inspection, but not the annual
B) The annual inspection, because they hold both ratings
C) Neither inspection
D) The annual, if a second mechanic countersigns
notes.choicesExplained: B (The annual inspection, because they hold both ratings): overlooks that the annual needs an IA. C (Neither inspection): overlooks the 100-hour privilege of both ratings. D (The annual, if a second mechanic countersigns): has no basis in part 65.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.85 Airframe rating; additional privileges
notes.evidence: In addition, he may perform the 100-hour inspection required by part 91 of this chapter on an airframe, or any related part or appliance, and approve and return it to service.

notes.front: A mechanic completes a major repair to a wing spar on a normal-category aeroplane, using approved data. Who may approve it for return to service, among these?
notes.back: A mechanic holding an inspection authorisation
notes.explanation: § 65.95(a)(1) lets the IA holder inspect and approve for return to service after a major repair done with approved data.
notes.choices:
A) The mechanic who did it, under the airframe rating
B) A mechanic holding an inspection authorisation
C) A powerplant-rated mechanic
D) The aircraft owner
notes.choicesExplained: A (The mechanic who did it, under the airframe rating): is excluded: airframe return-to-service privileges exclude major repairs. C (A powerplant-rated mechanic): has no privilege over airframe major repairs. D (The aircraft owner): has no return-to-service authority under part 65.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.95 Inspection authorization: Privileges and limitations
notes.evidence: (1) Inspect and approve for return to service any aircraft or related part or appliance (except any aircraft maintained in accordance with a continuous airworthiness program under part 121 of this chapter) after a major repair or major alteration to it

notes.front: Where must a mechanic keep their certificate, and for whom must they present it on request?
notes.back: Within the immediate area where they normally work under it, ready to present for inspection on request.
notes.explanation: The certificate must be at hand where the work is done.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.89 Display of certificate
notes.evidence: Each person who holds a mechanic certificate shall keep it within the immediate area where he normally exercises the privileges of the certificate and shall present it for inspection upon

notes.front: A local police officer at the hangar asks to see a mechanic's certificate. What must the mechanic do?
notes.back: Present it for inspection
notes.explanation: § 65.89 includes any federal, state or local law enforcement officer among those who may ask.
notes.choices:
A) Refuse, as only the Administrator may ask
B) Present it only if a National Transportation Safety Board representative is present
C) Present it for inspection
D) Give a copy of the address change form instead
notes.choicesExplained: A (Refuse, as only the Administrator may ask): overlooks that law enforcement officers are listed. B (Present it only if a National Transportation Safety Board representative is present): adds a condition § 65.89 does not have. D (Give a copy of the address change form instead): is not what § 65.89 requires.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.89 Display of certificate
notes.evidence: the request of the Administrator or an authorized representative of the National Transportation Safety Board, or of any Federal, State, or local law enforcement officer.

notes.front: What certificate history must an IA applicant have?
notes.back: A currently effective mechanic certificate with both airframe and powerplant ratings, in effect for a total of at least 3 years.
notes.explanation: Both ratings are required; one alone does not qualify.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.91 Inspection authorization
notes.evidence: (1) Hold a currently effective mechanic certificate with both an airframe rating and a powerplant rating, each of which is currently effective and has been in effect for a total of at least 3 years;

notes.front: What recent activity must an IA applicant show?
notes.back: Active engagement in maintaining certificated aircraft for at least the 2-year period before applying.
notes.explanation: It sits alongside the 3 years of holding both ratings.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.91 Inspection authorization
notes.evidence: (2) Have been actively engaged, for at least the 2-year period before the date he applies, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained in accordance with this chapter;

notes.front: What must an IA applicant's fixed base of operations provide, and must it be where inspections happen?
notes.back: A place where they can be reached in person or by telephone in a normal working week; it need not be where they inspect.
notes.explanation: The rule is about being contactable, not about where the work takes place.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.91 Inspection authorization
notes.evidence: (3) Have a fixed base of operations at which he may be located in person or by telephone during a normal working week but it need not be the place where he will exercise his inspection authority;

notes.front: Besides experience and a fixed base, what two further things does § 65.91(c) require of an IA applicant?
notes.back: Available equipment, facilities and inspection data to inspect properly, and a passed written test on inspecting to safety standards.
notes.explanation: Both sit in § 65.91(c) alongside the experience and fixed-base rules.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.91 Inspection authorization
notes.evidence: (4) Have available to him the equipment, facilities, and inspection data necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or any related part or appliance; and (5) Pass a written test on his ability to inspect according to safety standards

notes.front: A mechanic has held both ratings for 6 years but spent the last 2 years in aircraft sales, doing no maintenance. Can they apply for an IA now?
notes.back: No; they have not been actively maintaining aircraft for the 2 years before applying
notes.explanation: § 65.91(c)(2) requires active engagement in maintaining aircraft for at least the 2 years before applying.
notes.choices:
A) Yes; 6 years with both ratings is double the 3 required
B) Yes, if they pass the IA written test
C) No; they must first hold the ratings for 10 years
D) No; they have not been actively maintaining aircraft for the 2 years before applying
notes.choicesExplained: A (Yes; 6 years with both ratings is double the 3 required): ignores the separate 2-year activity rule. B (Yes, if they pass the IA written test): overlooks that the test is only one of the requirements. C (No; they must first hold the ratings for 10 years): invents a period; the rule is 3 years.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.91 Inspection authorization
notes.evidence: (2) Have been actively engaged, for at least the 2-year period before the date he applies, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained in accordance with this chapter;

notes.front: After failing the IA written test, how long must an applicant wait to apply for retesting?
notes.back: At least 90 days after the date of failure.
notes.explanation: The wait runs from the date of the failed test.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.91 Inspection authorization
notes.evidence: An applicant who fails the test prescribed in paragraph (c)(5) of this section may not apply for retesting until at least 90 days after the date he failed the test.

notes.front: When does an inspection authorisation expire?
notes.back: On 31 March of each odd-numbered year.
notes.explanation: Every inspection authorisation shares this expiry date.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.92 Inspection authorization: Duration
notes.evidence: (a) Each inspection authorization expires on March 31 of each odd-numbered year.

notes.front: What must an IA holder also hold to exercise IA privileges?
notes.back: A currently effective mechanic certificate with currently effective airframe and powerplant ratings.
notes.explanation: The IA rests on the mechanic certificate and both of its ratings.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.92 Inspection authorization: Duration
notes.evidence: However, the holder may exercise the privileges of that authorization only while he holds a currently effective mechanic certificate with both a currently effective airframe rating and a currently effective powerplant rating.

notes.front: Besides being surrendered, suspended or revoked, what two events make an IA cease to be effective?
notes.back: The holder no longer has a fixed base of operation, or no longer has the required equipment, facilities and inspection data.
notes.explanation: Both were conditions for issuing the IA in the first place.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.92 Inspection authorization: Duration
notes.evidence: (2) The holder no longer has a fixed base of operation. (3) The holder no longer has the equipment, facilities, and inspection data required by § 65.91(c) (3) and (4) for issuance of his authorization.

notes.front: As an IA renewal activity, how many annual inspections count?
notes.back: At least one annual inspection for each 90 days the current authority was held.
notes.explanation: The count scales with how long the authority was held.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.93 Inspection authorization: Renewal
notes.evidence: (1) Performed at least one annual inspection for each 90 days that the applicant held the current authority; or

notes.front: As an IA renewal activity, how many major repairs or major alterations count?
notes.back: At least two for each 90 days the current authority was held.
notes.explanation: This count also scales with how long the authority was held.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.93 Inspection authorization: Renewal
notes.evidence: (2) Performed at least two major repairs or major alterations for each 90 days that the applicant held the current authority; or

notes.front: Which inspection-programme activity counts once towards IA renewal?
notes.back: Performing or supervising and approving at least one progressive inspection to the Administrator's standards.
notes.explanation: One progressive inspection is enough for this activity.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.93 Inspection authorization: Renewal
notes.evidence: (3) Performed or supervised and approved at least one progressive inspection in accordance with standards prescribed by the Administrator; or

notes.front: How long must a refresher course be to count towards IA renewal?
notes.back: Not less than 8 hours of instruction, in a course acceptable to the Administrator.
notes.explanation: It must be attended and successfully completed.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.93 Inspection authorization: Renewal
notes.evidence: (4) Attended and successfully completed a refresher course, acceptable to the Administrator, of not less than 8 hours of instruction; or

notes.front: Which test can serve as an IA renewal activity?
notes.back: An oral test by a Federal Aviation Administration inspector showing current knowledge of the applicable regulations and standards.
notes.explanation: The inspector checks that the holder's knowledge is current.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.93 Inspection authorization: Renewal
notes.evidence: (5) Passed an oral test by an FAA inspector to determine that the applicant’s knowledge of applicable regulations and standards is current.

notes.front: In a 2-year IA period, when must renewal activities be completed?
notes.back: One activity by 31 March of the first year, and one during the second year.
notes.explanation: Each year of the 2-year period needs its own completed activity.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.93 Inspection authorization: Renewal
notes.evidence: the applicant must show completion of one of the activities in paragraphs (a)(1) through (5) of this section by March 31 of the first year of the 2-year inspection authorization period, and completion of one of the five activities during the second year of the 2-year period:

notes.front: According to the handbook, may an IA combine partial renewal activities, such as two annual inspections and four major repair inspections?
notes.back: No; the regulations do not provide for mixing renewal activities.
notes.explanation: Each activity must be completed in full on its own.
notes.source: FAA, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook – General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), ch. 13 “Mechanic Privileges & Limitations”, “Section 65.93, Inspection Authorization: Renewal”, p. 13-5
notes.evidence: However, the regulations do not provide for the mixing of any of these renewal activities

notes.front: In the first year of the IA period, an IA holder's only renewal activity is a 6-hour refresher seminar acceptable to the Administrator. Does that meet the first-year requirement?
notes.back: No; the course must be at least 8 hours
notes.explanation: § 65.93(a)(4) counts only a refresher course of not less than 8 hours of instruction.
notes.choices:
A) No; the course must be at least 8 hours
B) Yes; any acceptable seminar counts
C) Yes, if the holder also does one major repair
D) No; refresher courses never count
notes.choicesExplained: B (Yes; any acceptable seminar counts): ignores the 8-hour minimum. C (Yes, if the holder also does one major repair): mixes activities, which the regulations do not provide for. D (No; refresher courses never count): overlooks § 65.93(a)(4).
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.93 Inspection authorization: Renewal
notes.evidence: (4) Attended and successfully completed a refresher course, acceptable to the Administrator, of not less than 8 hours of instruction;

notes.front: Under § 65.95(a)(1), on what condition may an IA approve an aircraft for return to service after a major repair or alteration?
notes.back: The work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator.
notes.explanation: The approved-data condition applies to the major repair or alteration being approved.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.95 Inspection authorization: Privileges and limitations
notes.evidence: after a major repair or major alteration to it in accordance with part 43 [New] of this chapter, if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator;

notes.front: Which inspections may an IA perform under § 65.95(a)(2)?
notes.back: An annual inspection, and perform or supervise a progressive inspection.
notes.explanation: These inspections are made according to §§ 43.13 and 43.15.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.95 Inspection authorization: Privileges and limitations
notes.evidence: (2) Perform an annual, or perform or supervise a progressive inspection according to §§ 43.13 and 43.15 of this chapter.

notes.front: If an IA holder changes their fixed base of operation, what must they do before exercising IA privileges again?
notes.back: Notify, in writing, the responsible Flight Standards office for the new base's area.
notes.explanation: Until that notice is given, the IA privileges may not be exercised.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.95 Inspection authorization: Privileges and limitations
notes.evidence: (c) If the holder of an inspection authorization changes his fixed base of operation, he may not exercise the privileges of the authorization until he has notified the responsible Flight Standards office or International Field Office for the area in which the new base is located, in writing, of the change.

notes.front: What is the fundamental difference between a mechanic certificate and a repairman certificate?
notes.back: The mechanic certificate is transportable and not tied to a location; a repairman certificate is issued for work at a specific company location.
notes.explanation: Both rest on the technician's training and knowledge.
notes.source: FAA, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook – General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), ch. 13 “Mechanic Privileges & Limitations”, “Mechanic Privileges & Limitations”, p. 13-1
notes.evidence: the mechanic certificate is transportable, is issued to the technician based upon their training and knowledge, and is not dependent on the technician’s location. Although the repairman certificate is also based upon the training and knowledge of the technician, it is specifically issued to that technician while they are employed at a distinct location of a specific company.

notes.front: When does a repairman certificate stop being effective, if not surrendered, suspended or revoked sooner?
notes.back: When the holder is relieved from the duties for which they were employed and certificated.
notes.explanation: Leaving the job it was issued for ends it.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.15 Duration of certificates
notes.evidence: (b) Unless it is sooner surrendered, suspended, or revoked, a repairman certificate is effective until the holder is relieved from the duties for which the holder was employed and certificated.

notes.front: Besides monetary gain, what are two common ways the handbook says unethical behaviour is rationalised?
notes.back: Any two of: pretending it is not unethical; claiming it serves the organisation; assuming no one will find out (among others).
notes.explanation: The list ends with expecting superiors to support and protect you.
notes.source: FAA, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook – General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), ch. 13 “Mechanic Privileges & Limitations”, “Ethics”, p. 13-7
notes.evidence: Pretending that the behavior is not unethical or illegal. • Excusing the behavior by saying it is really in the organization’s (or the technician’s) best interest. • Assuming the behavior is okay, because no one else would even be expected to find out about it. • Expecting your superiors to support and protect you

notes.front: In the handbook's checklist for an ethical decision, what are the first three steps?
notes.back: Recognise and clarify the dilemma; get all the possible facts; list all the options.
notes.explanation: Every option is listed, not only the obvious ones, before any is judged.
notes.source: FAA, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook – General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), ch. 13 “Mechanic Privileges & Limitations”, “Ethics”, p. 13-8
notes.evidence: Recognize and clarify the dilemma. 2. Get all the possible facts. 3. List options—all of them.

notes.front: In the Professional Aviation Maintenance Association code of ethics the handbook recommends, what does the technician pledge about work beyond their knowledge?
notes.back: Never to undertake or approve work they believe is beyond the limits of their knowledge.
notes.explanation: The code accepts that no one has knowledge and skill in every aspect of maintenance for every aeroplane.
notes.source: FAA, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook – General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), ch. 13 “Mechanic Privileges & Limitations”, “Ethics”, p. 13-8
notes.evidence: “As a certified technician, I am aware that it is not possible to have knowledge and skill in every aspect of aviation maintenance for every airplane, so I pledge that I will never undertake work or approve work which I believe to be beyond the limits of my knowledge.

notes.front: According to the handbook, once a technician has removed a damaged part, can it be reinstalled because no replacement is in stock?
notes.back: No; once removal is committed, the part is unairworthy, whatever its deferability under the minimum equipment list.
notes.explanation: Correct documentation records the removal, then the installation of an airworthy part.
notes.source: FAA, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook – General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), ch. 13 “Mechanic Privileges & Limitations”, “Ethics”, p. 13-6
notes.evidence: The steps in properly documenting a maintenance event are to record the removal of the damaged part, then document the installation of an airworthy part. Once the technician has committed to removing the damaged part, it becomes unairworthy and cannot be reinstalled regardless of its deferability in the minimum equipment list (MEL).

notes.front: What responsibility does the handbook place on the mechanic when policy is bypassed to make an on-time departure?
notes.back: To follow the regulations and question the actions of their supervisors.
notes.explanation: The duty arises when policy is sidestepped for the sake of the schedule.
notes.source: FAA, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook – General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), ch. 13 “Mechanic Privileges & Limitations”, “Ethics”, p. 13-7
notes.evidence: It is the responsibility of the mechanic to follow regulations and to question the actions of their supervisors if the policy is circumvented to make an on-time

notes.front: A shift lead asks a mechanic to sign off a repair the mechanic doubts is airworthy, so the aircraft can leave on time. What does the Professional Aviation Maintenance Association code the handbook recommends say?
notes.back: Do not let a superior persuade you to approve work you doubt
notes.explanation: The code's pledge is not to let any superior persuade the technician to approve aircraft as airworthy when in doubt.
notes.choices:
A) Sign, since the superior carries the responsibility
B) Do not let a superior persuade you to approve work you doubt
C) Sign, then report it afterwards
D) Sign if no one is likely to find out
notes.choicesExplained: A (Sign, since the superior carries the responsibility): is the rationalisation of expecting superiors' protection. C (Sign, then report it afterwards): still approves work the mechanic doubts. D (Sign if no one is likely to find out): is another rationalisation the handbook lists.
notes.source: FAA, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook – General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), ch. 13 “Mechanic Privileges & Limitations”, “Ethics”, p. 13-8
notes.evidence: I shall not allow any superior to persuade me to approve aircraft or equipment as airworthy when there is doubt in my mind as to the validity of my action.

notes.front: An applicant with no AMTS document has 10 months of documented airframe experience and wants to sit the Airframe written test now. May they?
notes.back: No; they must first meet the experience requirements of § 65.77
notes.choices:
A) Yes; written tests have no prerequisites
B) Yes, once they have passed the oral test
C) No; they must first meet the experience requirements of § 65.77
D) No; they must first be 21 years old
notes.choicesExplained: A (Yes; written tests have no prerequisites): ignores § 65.75(a). B (Yes, once they have passed the oral test): reverses the order: the written test comes before the oral test.
