D (No; they must first be 21 years old): invents an age bar; the certificate itself needs an age of 18.
notes.explanation: § 65.75(a) puts the written test after the § 65.77 experience, at least 18 months for one rating; the early route in § 65.75(c) needs an AMTS document.
notes.evidence: (a) Except as specified in paragraph (c) of this section, each applicant for a mechanic certificate or rating must, after meeting the applicable experience requirements of § 65.77, pass a written test, appropriate to the rating sought
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.75 Knowledge requirements

notes.front: An applicant who is not an AMTS student has passed every section of the written test except one. What must happen before they apply for the oral and practical tests?
notes.back: They must pass the failed section
notes.choices:
A) Nothing; passing most sections is enough
B) They must pass the failed section
C) They must wait 24 months
D) They must first pass the oral test
notes.choicesExplained: A (Nothing; passing most sections is enough): ignores the word “each” in § 65.75(b). C (They must wait 24 months): confuses this with the 24-month period for passing all the tests. D (They must first pass the oral test): is circular: the oral test cannot be applied for until each written section is passed.
notes.explanation: § 65.75(b) requires each section of the written test to be passed before applying for the oral and practical tests.
notes.evidence: (b) The applicant must pass each section of the test before applying for the oral and practical tests prescribed by § 65.79. A report of the written test is sent to the applicant.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.75 Knowledge requirements

notes.front: A graduate of a certificated AMTS has no work experience. What can they present under § 65.77 instead of documented practical experience?
notes.back: An authenticated document from the school, issued under § 147.21
notes.choices:
A) A reference letter from an instructor
B) Their secondary school diploma
C) Nothing; 18 months of experience is still needed
D) An authenticated document from the school, issued under § 147.21
notes.choicesExplained: A (A reference letter from an instructor): is not the authenticated school document § 65.77 names. B (Their secondary school diploma): has nothing to do with aviation maintenance training. C (Nothing; 18 months of experience is still needed): overlooks the school document, the alternative to experience.
notes.explanation: § 65.77 accepts either an authenticated document from a certificated AMTS or documentary evidence of practical experience.
notes.evidence: Each applicant for a mechanic certificate or rating must present either— (a) An authenticated document from a certificated aviation maintenance technician school in accordance with § 147.21 of this chapter;
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.77 Experience requirements

notes.front: An applicant for the powerplant rating has passed the written tests. What must they still pass?
notes.back: An oral test and a practical test for the powerplant rating
notes.choices:
A) An oral test and a practical test for the powerplant rating
B) A practical test only
C) An oral test only
D) A second written test on regulations
notes.choicesExplained: B (A practical test only): leaves out the oral test. C (An oral test only): leaves out the practical test. D (A second written test on regulations): is not something § 65.79 requires.
notes.explanation: § 65.79 requires both an oral test and a practical test, as appropriate to the rating sought.
notes.evidence: Each applicant for a mechanic certificate or rating must pass an oral test and a practical test, as appropriate to the rating sought, by demonstrating satisfactory understanding of the knowledge, risk management, and skill elements for each subject
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.79 Skill requirements

notes.front: An ACS element begins with the word “Identify”. What type of element is it, and on which tests is it assessed?
notes.back: Risk management; oral and practical tests
notes.choices:
A) Knowledge; written and oral tests
B) Skill; practical test only
C) Risk management; oral and practical tests
D) Knowledge; written test only
notes.choicesExplained: A (Knowledge; written and oral tests): knowledge elements begin “Exhibits knowledge in…”. B (Skill; practical test only): skill elements begin “Demonstrates the skill to perform…”. D (Knowledge; written test only): has the wrong type, and knowledge is also tested orally.
notes.explanation: The Companion Guide marks risk management elements with words such as “Determine, Identify, Creates” and assesses them on the oral and practical tests.
notes.evidence: Risk—(oral test, practical test) elements are indicated by the use of the words, “Determine, Identify, Creates…"
notes.source: FAA, Companion Guide to the Aviation Mechanic ACS (FAA-G-ACS-1, with Changes 1 and 2), “Chapter 2: How to Use the ACS”, p. 11

notes.front: An applicant plans 2 minutes per question on the Aviation Mechanic General written test. Does that fit the time allowed?
notes.back: Yes, exactly: 60 questions take 120 minutes, the 2.0 hours allowed
notes.choices:
A) No; 100 questions would need 200 minutes
B) Yes, exactly: 60 questions take 120 minutes, the 2.0 hours allowed
C) No; only 1 hour is allowed
D) Yes, with an hour to spare
notes.choicesExplained: A (No; 100 questions would need 200 minutes): uses the 100 questions of the Airframe and Powerplant tests. C (No; only 1 hour is allowed): the time allowed is 2.0 hours, not 1. D (Yes, with an hour to spare): 120 minutes fills the 2.0 hours, leaving none to spare.
notes.explanation: The General test has 60 questions in 2.0 hours, so 60 × 2 = 120 minutes uses the whole time.
notes.evidence: AMG Aviation Mechanic Technician - 60 N/A 2.0 70 General AMA Aviation Mechanic Technician - 100 N/A 2.0 70 Airframe
notes.source: FAA, Companion Guide to the Aviation Mechanic ACS (FAA-G-ACS-1, with Changes 1 and 2), “Chapter 3: Written Test Description”, p. 12

notes.front: On the 60-question General written test, an applicant answers 42 correctly. Taking the grade as the percentage answered correctly, have they passed?
notes.back: Yes; 42 of 60 is 70 percent, the minimum passing grade
notes.choices:
A) No; a grade must be above 70 percent
B) No; 42 of 60 is 60 percent
C) No; the minimum is 75 percent
D) Yes; 42 of 60 is 70 percent, the minimum passing grade
notes.choicesExplained: A (No; a grade must be above 70 percent): misreads “minimum”: 70 percent itself passes. B (No; 42 of 60 is 60 percent): miscalculates: 42 ÷ 60 is 0.70. C (No; the minimum is 75 percent): the minimum passing grade is 70 percent.
notes.explanation: 42 ÷ 60 = 0.70, or 70 percent, and § 65.17(b) makes 70 percent the minimum passing grade, so 70 percent passes.
notes.evidence: (b) The minimum passing grade for each test is 70 percent.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.17 Tests: General procedure

notes.front: Under § 65.81(a), which task may a mechanic holding only the airframe rating perform?
notes.back: Replacing a damaged wing fairing
notes.choices:
A) Replacing a damaged wing fairing
B) Repairing an airspeed indicator
C) A major alteration of a propeller
D) Overhauling an engine cylinder
notes.choicesExplained: B (Repairing an airspeed indicator): any repair of instruments is excluded from every mechanic's privileges. C (A major alteration of a propeller): major propeller alterations are excluded too, and propellers belong to the powerplant rating. D (Overhauling an engine cylinder): engine work needs the powerplant rating.
notes.explanation: § 65.81(a) lets a mechanic perform or supervise maintenance of the aircraft or parts for which they are rated, and a wing fairing is part of the airframe.
notes.evidence: (a) A certificated mechanic may perform or supervise the maintenance, preventive maintenance or alteration of an aircraft or appliance, or a part thereof, for which he is rated
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.81 General privileges and limitations

notes.front: An airframe-rated mechanic completes a minor repair to a flap skin. Who may approve the flap for return to service?
notes.back: The airframe mechanic who did the repair
notes.choices:
A) Only a mechanic holding an inspection authorisation
B) The airframe mechanic who did the repair
C) Only a powerplant-rated mechanic
D) Only the aircraft owner
notes.choicesExplained: A (Only a mechanic holding an inspection authorisation): an inspection authorisation is needed only after a major repair or alteration. C (Only a powerplant-rated mechanic): a flap is an airframe part, outside the powerplant rating. D (Only the aircraft owner): an owner has no return-to-service privilege under part 65.
notes.explanation: § 65.85(a) lets an airframe-rated mechanic approve an airframe part for return to service after performing its maintenance, major repairs and alterations excepted.
notes.evidence: a certificated mechanic with an airframe rating may approve and return to service an airframe, or any related part or appliance, after he has performed, supervised, or inspected its maintenance or alteration (excluding major repairs and major alterations).
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.85 Airframe rating; additional privileges

notes.front: A mechanic holding only the powerplant rating completes a 100-hour inspection of an aircraft's engine and propeller. What may they approve for return to service?
notes.back: The engine and propeller
notes.choices:
A) The whole aircraft, including the airframe
B) Nothing without an inspection authorisation
C) The engine and propeller
D) The engine only; propellers need a repairman
notes.choicesExplained: A (The whole aircraft, including the airframe): the airframe needs the airframe rating. B (Nothing without an inspection authorisation): a 100-hour inspection does not need an inspection authorisation. D (The engine only; propellers need a repairman): the powerplant rating covers propellers too.
notes.explanation: § 65.87(a) lets a powerplant-rated mechanic perform the 100-hour inspection on a powerplant or propeller and approve it for return to service.
notes.evidence: In addition, he may perform the 100-hour inspection required by part 91 of this chapter on a powerplant or propeller, or any part thereof, and approve and return it to service.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.87 Powerplant rating; additional privileges

notes.front: An inspection authorisation is issued in June 2025. When does it expire, unless it ends sooner?
notes.back: 31 March 2027
notes.choices:
A) 31 March 2027
B) June 2027
C) 31 March 2026
D) It never expires
notes.choicesExplained: B (June 2027): counts two years from the date of issue instead. C (31 March 2026): 2026 is an even-numbered year. D (It never expires): confuses the inspection authorisation with the mechanic certificate, which does not expire.
notes.explanation: Every inspection authorisation expires on 31 March of an odd-numbered year, and the first such date after June 2025 is 31 March 2027.
notes.evidence: (a) Each inspection authorization expires on March 31 of each odd-numbered year.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 65 (1 January 2025 edition), § 65.92 Inspection authorization: Duration
